verses.original: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Ēn de tis asthenōn Lazaros apo Bēthanias ek tēs kōmēs Marias kai Marthas tēs adelphēs autēs
verses.literal: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick He lived in Bethany the village of Mary and her sister Martha
verses.literalPt: Estava doente um homem chamado Lázaro, de Betânia, da aldeia de Maria e sua irmã Marta.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν Κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει
verses.transliteration: ēn de Mariam hē aleipsasa ton Kyrion myrō kai ekmaxasa tous podas autou tais thrixin autēs hēs ho adelphos Lazaros ēsthenei
verses.literal: ( Mary whose brother Lazarus was sick was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair
verses.literalPt: Maria, cujo irmão Lázaro se achava doente, era a que ungira o Senhor com perfume e lhe enxugara os pés com os seus cabelos.

verses.original: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι Κύριε ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ
verses.transliteration: apesteilan oun hai adelphai pros auton legousai Kyrie ide hon phileis asthenei
verses.literal: So the sisters sent word to Jesus Lord . . . the one You love is sick
verses.literalPt: Mandaram, pois, as irmãs de Lázaro dizer a Jesus: Senhor, aquele que amas está doente.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλ’ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ δι’ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Akousas de ho Iēsous eipen Hautē hē astheneia ouk estin pros thanaton all’ hyper tēs doxēs tou Theou hina doxasthē ho Huios tou Theou di’ autēs
verses.literal: When Jesus heard this He said This sickness will not end in death No it is for the glory of God so that the Son of God may be glorified through it
verses.literalPt: Ao saber isso, disse Jesus: Esta doença não é para morte, mas para a glória de Deus, a fim de que o Filho de Deus seja por ela glorificado.

verses.original: Ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον
verses.transliteration: Ēgapa de ho Iēsous tēn Marthan kai tēn adelphēn autēs kai ton Lazaron
verses.literal: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus
verses.literalPt: Ora, Jesus estimava a Marta, e a sua irmã, e a Lázaro.

verses.original: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας
verses.transliteration: hōs oun ēkousen hoti asthenei tote men emeinen en hō ēn topō dyo hēmeras
verses.literal: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick - He stayed where He was for two days
verses.literalPt: Tendo sabido, pois, que este estava doente, demorou-se ainda dois dias no lugar onde se achava.

verses.original: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν
verses.transliteration: epeita meta touto legei tois mathētais Agōmen eis tēn Ioudaian palin
verses.literal: and then . . . . . . He said to the disciples Let us go back to Judea
verses.literalPt: Então, passado isso, disse aos discípulos: Voltemos para a Judeia.

verses.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί Ῥαββί νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ
verses.transliteration: Legousin autō hoi mathētai Rhabbi nyn ezētoun se lithasai hoi Ioudaioi kai palin hypageis ekei
verses.literal: Rabbi they replied the Jews just tried to stone You and You are going back there
verses.literalPt: Perguntaram estes: Mestre, agora mesmo os judeus procuravam apedrejar-te, e voltas ainda para lá?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσιν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ οὐ προσκόπτει ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē Iēsous Ouchi dōdeka hōrai eisin tēs hēmeras ean tis peripatē en tē hēmera ou proskoptei hoti to phōs tou kosmou toutou blepei
verses.literal: Jesus answered Are there not twelve hours of daylight If anyone walks in the daytime he will not stumble because he sees by the light of this world
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Jesus: Não são doze as horas do dia? Se alguém andar de dia, não tropeça, porque vê a luz deste mundo;

verses.original: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί προσκόπτει ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: ean de tis peripatē en tē nykti proskoptei hoti to phōs ouk estin en autō
verses.literal: But if anyone walks at night he will stumble because he has no light
verses.literalPt: mas, se alguém andar de noite, tropeça, porque a luz não está nele.

verses.original: Ταῦτα εἶπεν καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Tauta eipen kai meta touto legei autois Lazaros ho philos hēmōn kekoimētai alla poreuomai hina exypnisō auton
verses.literal: After He had said this He told them Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep but I am going there to wake him up . . .
verses.literalPt: Assim falou e depois lhes disse: Nosso amigo Lázaro dorme, mas vou despertá-lo do sono.

verses.original: Εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ κεκοίμηται σωθήσεται
verses.transliteration: Eipan oun hoi mathētai autō Kyrie ei kekoimētai sōthēsetai
verses.literal: His disciples replied Lord if he is sleeping he will get better
verses.literalPt: Disseram-lhe, então, os discípulos: Senhor, se dorme, ficará bom.

verses.original: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει
verses.transliteration: eirēkei de ho Iēsous peri tou thanatou autou ekeinoi de edoxan hoti peri tēs koimēseōs tou hypnou legei
verses.literal: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep . . . . . . but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus
verses.literalPt: Jesus tinha falado da morte de Lázaro; mas eles supunham que falasse do repouso do sono.

verses.original: Τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν
verses.transliteration: Tote oun eipen autois ho Iēsous parrēsia Lazaros apethanen
verses.literal: So Jesus told them plainly Lazarus is dead
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes, pois, Jesus abertamente: Lázaro morreu;

verses.original: καὶ χαίρω δι’ ὑμᾶς ἵνα πιστεύσητε ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: kai chairō di’ hymas hina pisteusēte hoti ouk ēmēn ekei alla agōmen pros auton
verses.literal: and for your sake . . . I am glad I was not there so that you may believe But let us go to him
verses.literalPt: e, por vossa causa, folgo de não me achar lá, para que creiais; mas vamos ter com ele.

verses.original: Εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συμμαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Eipen oun Thōmas ho legomenos Didymos tois symmathētais Agōmen kai hēmeis hina apothanōmen met’ autou
verses.literal: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples Let us also go so that we may die with Him
verses.literalPt: Então, Tomé, chamado Dídimo, disse aos seus condiscípulos: Vamos também nós, para morrermos com ele.

verses.original: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ
verses.transliteration: Elthōn oun ho Iēsous heuren auton tessaras ēdē hēmeras echonta en tō mnēmeiō
verses.literal: When Jesus arrived He found that Lazarus had already spent . . . four days in the tomb
verses.literalPt: Chegando Jesus, achou que estava Lázaro no túmulo havia já quatro dias.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ ἡ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε
verses.transliteration: ēn de hē Bēthania engys tōn Hierosolymōn hōs apo stadiōn dekapente
verses.literal: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem a little less than two miles . . . away
verses.literalPt: Ora, Betânia distava de Jerusalém cerca de quinze estádios.

verses.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ Μαριὰμ ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ
verses.transliteration: polloi de ek tōn Ioudaiōn elēlytheisan pros tēn Marthan kai Mariam hina paramythēsōntai autas peri tou adelphou
verses.literal: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother
verses.literalPt: Muitos dos judeus tinham vindo ter com Marta e Maria, para as consolar pela morte de seu irmão.

verses.original: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ Μαριὰμ δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο
verses.transliteration: hē oun Martha hōs ēkousen hoti Iēsous erchetai hypēntēsen autō Mariam de en tō oikō ekathezeto
verses.literal: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming she went out to meet Him but Mary stayed at home
verses.literalPt: Marta, quando soube que vinha Jesus, foi encontrá-lo; Maria, porém, ficou sentada em casa.

verses.original: Εἶπεν οὖν ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν Κύριε εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου
verses.transliteration: Eipen oun hē Martha pros ton Iēsoun Kyrie ei ēs hōde ouk an apethanen ho adelphos mou
verses.literal: Martha said to Jesus Lord if You had been here my brother would not have died
verses.literalPt: Disse, então, Marta a Jesus: Senhor, se tivesses estado aqui, não teria morrido meu irmão.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν Θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ Θεός
verses.transliteration: alla kai nyn oida hoti hosa an aitēsē ton Theon dōsei soi ho Theos
verses.literal: But . . . even now I know that God will give You whatever . . . You ask of Him
verses.literalPt: E mesmo agora sei que tudo o que pedires a Deus Deus to dará.

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου
verses.transliteration: Legei autē ho Iēsous Anastēsetai ho adelphos sou
verses.literal: Your brother will rise again Jesus told her
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhe Jesus: Teu irmão há de ressuscitar.

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ
verses.transliteration: Legei autō hē Martha Oida hoti anastēsetai en tē anastasei en tē eschatē hēmera
verses.literal: Martha replied . . . I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day
verses.literalPt: Eu sei, replicou Marta, que ele há de ressuscitar na ressurreição, no último dia.

verses.original: Εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται
verses.transliteration: Eipen autē ho Iēsous Egō eimi hē anastasis kai hē zōē ho pisteuōn eis eme kan apothanē zēsetai
verses.literal: Jesus said to her I am the resurrection and the life Whoever believes in Me will live even though he dies
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhe Jesus: Eu sou a ressurreição e a vida. O que crê em mim, ainda que esteja morto, viverá;

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα πιστεύεις τοῦτο
verses.transliteration: kai pas ho zōn kai pisteuōn eis eme ou mē apothanē eis ton aiōna pisteueis touto
verses.literal: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die . . . . . . . . . Do you believe this
verses.literalPt: e todo o que vive e crê em mim nunca jamais morrerá. Crês isso?

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος
verses.transliteration: Legei autō Nai Kyrie egō pepisteuka hoti sy ei ho Christos ho Huios tou Theou ho eis ton kosmon erchomenos
verses.literal: Yes Lord she answered . . . I believe that You are the Christ the Son of God who was to come into the world
verses.literalPt: Sim, Senhor, respondeu ela, eu creio que tu és o Cristo, o Filho de Deus que havia de vir ao mundo.

verses.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα Ὁ Διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε
verses.transliteration: Kai touto eipousa apēlthen kai ephōnēsen Mariam tēn adelphēn autēs lathra eipousa Ho Didaskalos parestin kai phōnei se
verses.literal: After Martha had said this she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her The Teacher is here and is asking for you
verses.literalPt: Tendo dito isso, foi ela chamar a Maria, sua irmã, e lhe disse em particular: Está aí o Mestre e te chama.

verses.original: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: ekeinē de hōs ēkousen ēgerthē tachy kai ērcheto pros auton
verses.literal: And when Mary heard this she got up quickly and went to Him
verses.literalPt: Ela, ouvindo isso, levantou-se depressa e foi ter com ele

verses.original: Οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην ἀλλ’ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα
verses.transliteration: Oupō de elēlythei ho Iēsous eis tēn kōmēn all’ ēn eti en tō topō hopou hypēntēsen autō hē Martha
verses.literal: Now Jesus had not yet entered . . . the village but was still at the place where Martha had met Him
verses.literalPt: (pois Jesus não havia ainda entrado na aldeia, mas permanecia no lugar onde Marta o encontrara).

verses.original: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ
verses.transliteration: hoi oun Ioudaioi hoi ontes met’ autēs en tē oikia kai paramythoumenoi autēn idontes tēn Mariam hoti tacheōs anestē kai exēlthen ēkolouthēsan autē doxantes hoti hypagei eis to mnēmeion hina klausē ekei
verses.literal: When the Jews who were in the house consoling - Mary saw how quickly - she got up and went out they followed her supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there
verses.literalPt: Os judeus que estavam com Maria em casa e a consolavam, vendo-a levantar-se depressa e partir, seguiram-na, pensando que ela ia ao túmulo para ali chorar.

verses.original: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας λέγουσα αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός
verses.transliteration: hē oun Mariam hōs ēlthen hopou ēn Iēsous idousa auton epesen autou pros tous podas legousa autō Kyrie ei ēs hōde ouk an mou apethanen ho adelphos
verses.literal: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him she fell at His feet and said Lord if You had been here my brother would not have died
verses.literalPt: Quando Maria chegou ao lugar onde estava Jesus, ao vê-lo, lançou-se-lhe aos pés, dizendo: Senhor, se tivesses estado aqui, não teria morrido meu irmão.

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν
verses.transliteration: Iēsous oun hōs eiden autēn klaiousan kai tous synelthontas autē Ioudaious klaiontas enebrimēsato tō pneumati kai etaraxen heauton
verses.literal: When Jesus saw her weeping and the Jews who had come with her also weeping He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled
verses.literalPt: Jesus, vendo-a chorar e chorar também os judeus que a acompanhavam, gemeu em espírito, perturbou-se

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε
verses.transliteration: kai eipen Pou tetheikate auton Legousin autō Kyrie erchou kai ide
verses.literal: Where have you put him He asked Come and see Lord they answered . . .
verses.literalPt: e perguntou: Onde o pusestes? Eles lhe responderam: Senhor, vem e vê.

verses.original: Ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς
verses.transliteration: Edakrysen ho Iēsous
verses.literal: Jesus wept
verses.literalPt: Jesus chorou.

verses.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Elegon oun hoi Ioudaioi Ide pōs ephilei auton
verses.literal: Then the Jews said See how He loved him
verses.literalPt: Os judeus, então, diziam: Vede como ele o amava!

verses.original: Τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ
verses.transliteration: Tines de ex autōn eipan Ouk edynato houtos ho anoixas tous ophthalmous tou typhlou poiēsai hina kai houtos mē apothanē
verses.literal: But some of them asked Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept . . . Lazarus from dying
verses.literalPt: Mas alguns deles disseram: Não podia este homem, que abriu os olhos ao cego, fazer que este não morresse?

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπ’ αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Iēsous oun palin embrimōmenos en heautō erchetai eis to mnēmeion ēn de spēlaion kai lithos epekeito ep’ autō
verses.literal: Jesus once again deeply moved . . . . . . came to the tomb It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance
verses.literalPt: Jesus, gemendo outra vez em si mesmo, foi ao túmulo; era este uma gruta, a cuja entrada estava posta uma pedra.

verses.original: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα Κύριε ἤδη ὄζει τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: legei ho Iēsous Arate ton lithon Legei autō hē adelphē tou teteleutēkotos Martha Kyrie ēdē ozei tetartaios gar estin
verses.literal: Take away the stone Jesus said Lord by now he stinks said Martha the sister of the dead man It has already been four days
verses.literalPt: Jesus disse: Tirai a pedra. Disse-lhe Marta, irmã do morto: Senhor, ele já cheira mal; porque está morto há quatro dias.

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Legei autē ho Iēsous Ouk eipon soi hoti ean pisteusēs opsē tēn doxan tou Theou
verses.literal: Jesus replied . . . Did I not tell you that if you believed you would see the glory of God
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhe Jesus: Não te disse eu que, se creres, verás a glória de Deus?

verses.original: Ἦραν οὖν τὸν λίθον ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν Πάτερ εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου
verses.transliteration: Ēran oun ton lithon ho de Iēsous ēren tous ophthalmous anō kai eipen Pater eucharistō soi hoti ēkousas mou
verses.literal: So they took away the stone Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said Father I thank You that You have heard Me
verses.literalPt: Tiraram, então, a pedra. Jesus, levantando os olhos, disse: Pai, graças te dou que me ouviste.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας
verses.transliteration: egō de ēdein hoti pantote mou akoueis alla dia ton ochlon ton periestōta eipon hina pisteusōsin hoti sy me apesteilas
verses.literal: I knew that You always hear Me but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here so they may believe that You sent Me
verses.literalPt: Eu sabia que sempre me ouves, mas assim falei por causa desta multidão que me cerca, a fim de crerem que tu me enviaste.

verses.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν Λάζαρε δεῦρο ἔξω
verses.transliteration: Kai tauta eipōn phōnē megalē ekraugasen Lazare deuro exō
verses.literal: After Jesus had said this He called out in a loud voice Lazarus come out
verses.literalPt: Tendo assim falado, clamou em alta voz: Lázaro, sai para fora!

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν
verses.transliteration: exēlthen ho tethnēkōs dedemenos tous podas kai tas cheiras keiriais kai hē opsis autou soudariō periededeto Legei autois ho Iēsous Lysate auton kai aphete auton hypagein
verses.literal: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen and his face wrapped in a cloth Unwrap him and let him go Jesus told them
verses.literalPt: Saiu aquele que estivera morto, ligados os pés e as mãos com faixas e envolto o seu rosto em um lenço. Disse-lhes Jesus: Desatai-o e deixai-o ir.

verses.original: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ἃ ἐποίησεν ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Polloi oun ek tōn Ioudaiōn hoi elthontes pros tēn Mariam kai theasamenoi ha epoiēsen episteusan eis auton
verses.literal: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary and had seen what Jesus did believed in Him
verses.literalPt: Muitos dos judeus que vieram ter com Maria e viram o que fizera Jesus creram nele.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς
verses.transliteration: tines de ex autōn apēlthon pros tous Pharisaious kai eipan autois ha epoiēsen Iēsous
verses.literal: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done
verses.literalPt: Alguns deles, porém, foram ter com os fariseus e lhes contaram o que Jesus tinha feito.

verses.original: Συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον καὶ ἔλεγον Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα
verses.transliteration: Synēgagon oun hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi synedrion kai elegon Ti poioumen hoti houtos ho anthrōpos polla poiei sēmeia
verses.literal: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said What are we to do This man is performing many signs
verses.literalPt: Então, os principais sacerdotes e os fariseus convocaram uma reunião do Sinédrio e disseram: Que estamos fazendo, pois que esse homem faz muitos milagres?

verses.original: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος
verses.transliteration: ean aphōmen auton houtōs pantes pisteusousin eis auton kai eleusontai hoi Rhōmaioi kai arousin hēmōn kai ton topon kai to ethnos
verses.literal: If we let Him go on like this everyone will believe in Him and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation
verses.literalPt: Se o deixarmos assim, todos crerão nele; e virão os romanos e nos tirarão tanto o nosso lugar como a nossa nação.

verses.original: Εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν
verses.transliteration: Heis de tis ex autōn Kaiaphas archiereus ōn tou eniautou ekeinou eipen autois Hymeis ouk oidate ouden
verses.literal: But one of them named Caiaphas who was high priest that year said to them You know nothing at all
verses.literalPt: Caifás, porém, um dentre eles, sumo sacerdote naquele ano, disse-lhes: Vós nada sabeis,

verses.original: οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται
verses.transliteration: oude logizesthe hoti sympherei hymin hina heis anthrōpos apothanē hyper tou laou kai mē holon to ethnos apolētai
verses.literal: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish
verses.literalPt: nem considerais que vos convém que morra um só homem pelo povo e que não pereça toda a nação.

verses.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνήσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους
verses.transliteration: Touto de aph’ heautou ouk eipen alla archiereus ōn tou eniautou ekeinou eprophēteusen hoti emellen Iēsous apothnēskein hyper tou ethnous
verses.literal: Caiaphas did not say this on his own Instead as high priest that year he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation
verses.literalPt: Ora, ele não disse isso por si mesmo; mas, sendo sumo sacerdote daquele ano, profetizou que Jesus havia de morrer pela nação

verses.original: καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν
verses.transliteration: kai ouch hyper tou ethnous monon all’ hina kai ta tekna tou Theou ta dieskorpismena synagagē eis hen
verses.literal: and not only for the nation but also for the scattered children of God to gather them together into one
verses.literalPt: e não somente pela nação, mas também para reunir em um corpo os filhos de Deus, que estão dispersos.

verses.original: Ἀπ’ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Ap’ ekeinēs oun tēs hēmeras ebouleusanto hina apokteinōsin auton
verses.literal: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him
verses.literalPt: Desde aquele dia, resolveram tirar-lhe a vida.

verses.original: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν
verses.transliteration: HO oun Iēsous ouketi parrēsia periepatei en tois Ioudaiois alla apēlthen ekeithen eis tēn chōran engys tēs erēmou eis Ephraim legomenēn polin kakei emeinen meta tōn mathētōn
verses.literal: As a result Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews but He withdrew . . . to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness And He stayed there with the disciples
verses.literalPt: Assim, já não andava Jesus abertamente entre os judeus, mas retirou-se dali para uma região próxima do deserto, a uma cidade chamada Efraim; e ali ficou com os discípulos.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς
verses.transliteration: Ēn de engys to pascha tōn Ioudaiōn kai anebēsan polloi eis Hierosolyma ek tēs chōras pro tou pascha hina hagnisōsin heautous
verses.literal: Now the Jewish Passover was near and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover
verses.literalPt: Estava próxima a Páscoa dos judeus; e muitos subiram daquela região a Jerusalém antes da Páscoa, para se purificarem.

verses.original: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετ’ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν
verses.transliteration: ezētoun oun ton Iēsoun kai elegon met’ allēlōn en tō hierō hestēkotes Ti dokei hymin hoti ou mē elthē eis tēn heortēn
verses.literal: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts What do you think . . . Will He come to the feast at all
verses.literalPt: Procuravam a Jesus e perguntavam uns aos outros, estando no templo: Que vos parece? Não virá ele à festa?

verses.original: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: dedōkeisan de hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi entolas hina ean tis gnō pou estin mēnysē hopōs piasōsin auton
verses.literal: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it so that they could arrest Him
verses.literalPt: Ora, os principais sacerdotes e os fariseus tinham dado ordens que, se alguém soubesse onde ele estava, o denunciasse, para o prenderem.
